steps.tx: The genetic hallmark of Ewing sarcoma is the balanced reciprocal **chromosomal translocation** t(11;22)(q24;q12), identified in over eighty-five to ninety percent of cases. This structural rearrangement fuses the central exon of the EWSR1 gene on chromosome 22 with the DNA-binding domain of the FLI1 ETS transcription factor on chromosome 11. The resultant chimeric oncoprotein acts as a constitutively active aberrant transcription factor driving malignant neuroectodermal transformation.
steps.say: Ewing sarcoma is defined by the balanced reciprocal chromosomal translocation t(11;22). This rearranges chromosome 22 and 11, fusing the EWSR1 gene with the FLI1 transcription factor. The resulting chimeric protein acts as an abnormal transcription factor that drives uncontrollable neoplastic cell growth.

vis.title: Ewing Sarcoma Molecular Profile
rows: Present in 85 to 90 percent of Ewing family tumors
Present in 5 to 10 percent of variant cases

steps.tx: This labelled picture belongs to a tumour defined by a gene fusion rather than by where it grows. In **Ewing sarcoma**, the t(11;22) translocation joins EWSR1 to FLI1 and rewires transcription in a small round cell tumour of bone and soft tissue. Children present with pain, swelling and sometimes fever that mimics infection. Recognising the pattern matters because treatment is chemotherapy led, with surgery or radiation reserved for local control of the primary site.
steps.say: Ewing sarcoma is a small round cell tumour driven by the EWSR1 FLI1 fusion from t(11;22). Treatment is chemotherapy led, with local control by surgery or radiation.

steps.tx: Examine the femoral shaft on this plain film. Instead of one clean hole, the bone shows a moth eaten, permeative pattern of destruction, and the surface is wrapped in fine concentric layers of new bone. That layered **onion skin periosteal reaction** is the radiographic signature students associate with Ewing sarcoma in a child or teenager with a painful limb mass.
steps.say: On this femur film the shaft shows permeative destruction wrapped in layers of new surface bone. That onion skin periosteal reaction is the classic radiographic clue to Ewing sarcoma.

steps.tx: Histopathologically, Ewing sarcoma presents as a quintessential **small round blue cell** tumour displaying monotonous sheets of uniform round cells with hyperchromatic nuclei, minimal cytoplasm, and glycogen-positive periodic acid-Schiff staining. On immunohistochemistry, strong, diffuse, membranous expression of CD99 (MIC2 gene product) is virtually diagnostic, effectively distinguishing Ewing sarcoma from neuroblastoma, lymphoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma.
steps.say: Under the microscope, Ewing sarcoma is a classic small round blue cell tumor. It consists of sheets of identical round cells packed with clear glycogen that stains positive with PAS. Diffuse, intense membranous staining for CD99 on immunohistochemistry confirms the diagnosis and separates it from lymphoma and neuroblastoma.

left.title: Ewing Sarcoma Markers
points: PAS positive glycogen granules in cytoplasm

steps.tx: Radiographs display permeative, moth-eaten diaphyseal cortical bone destruction accompanied by the pathognomonic **onion skinning** periosteal reaction. As the tumor erupts through the cortical Haversian systems into the subperiosteal space, rapid cyclical elevation stimulates the periosteum to deposit multiple concentric, concentric layers of reactive bone. Extensive associated soft tissue masses are characteristic, often out-sizing the intraosseous destruction.
steps.say: On X-rays, look for a moth-eaten permeative lucency in the middle shaft of a long bone. The subperiosteal spread stimulates the periosteum to lay down multiple concentric parallel sheets of reactive bone, creating the classic onion skin appearance. There is almost always a huge soft tissue mass surrounding the bone.

vis.title: Radiographic Hallmarks of Ewing Sarcoma
rows: Cuff of reactive bone at margin
Large soft tissue shadow without bone

steps.tx: In mature adults, **chondrosarcoma** represents the primary non-osteogenic bone malignancy, characteristically arising in the pelvis, proximal femur, and shoulder girdle. Radiographs demonstrate an osteolytic lesion with central punctate, ring-and-arc, or popcorn-like calcifications reflecting its cartilaginous matrix. High-grade chondrosarcomas are notably chemo-resistant and radio-resistant, rendering wide surgical en bloc resection the only effective therapeutic modality.
steps.say: In adults over forty, chondrosarcoma is the commonest primary cartilage cancer, favoring the pelvis, upper femur, and ribs. Radiographs reveal an expansile lytic area peppered with punctate ring-and-arc or popcorn calcifications. Because cartilage cells do not respond to chemotherapy or radiation, wide surgical resection is the only curative treatment.

left.title: Chondrosarcoma Features
points: Peak incidence in adults 40 to 70 years

steps.tx: The assessment of secondary bone metastases relies on the **Mirels score** to quantify impending pathological fracture risk in long bones. The system assigns one to three points across four categories: anatomical site (upper limb, lower limb, peritrochanteric), nature of pain (mild, moderate, functional weight-bearing), radiographic lesion type (blastic, mixed, lytic), and cortical bone size. A score of nine or greater mandates prophylactic surgical internal fixation.
steps.say: The Mirels score predicts when a metastatic bone lesion is about to snap. It grades four variables from one to three points: location, pain severity, lytic versus blastic appearance, and size. Any score of nine or higher carries over thirty-three percent fracture risk and demands prophylactic surgical nailing before radiation.

quiz.q: Which chromosomal translocation is pathognomonic for Ewing sarcoma?
quiz.explain: The reciprocal translocation t(11;22)(q24;q12) produces the EWSR1-FLI1 fusion transcript in 85 to 90 percent of Ewing sarcoma cases.

quiz.q: According to the Mirels scoring system, what threshold score indicates the need for prophylactic internal fixation?
quiz.explain: A Mirels score of 9 or greater indicates a high risk of impending pathological fracture (>33%) and mandates prophylactic internal fixation before radiotherapy.
